obs: United States v. Wong Kim Ark

"The provision of that act, concerning 'the children of persons duly naturalized under any of the laws of the United States,' not being restricted to the children of persons already naturalized, might well be held to include children of persons thereafter to be naturalized."

"Petitioners premise, however, flies in the face of the widely accepted modern legislative drafting convention that a law should not be read to speak as of the date of enactment. ... A legislative provision speaks as of any date on which it is read (rather than as of when drafted, enacted, or put into effect)."
